summary: Describes a URN namespace run by OASIS for naming persistent resources stored in the XML.org repository, such as DTDs, schemas, namespaces, and stylesheets.

eli5.summary: It gives each file in a library a permanent name that does not change even if the shelf moves.

questions: how to reference xml resources permanently
subtitle: Assigning persistent names to XML resources.

tldr.problem: XML repositories need unique, permanent identifiers for resources like schemas and stylesheets that do not depend on where those files are stored.
tldr.mechanism: OASIS defines a URN namespace called xmlorg that assigns hierarchical names to XML documents based on their type and a unique object identifier.
tldr.outcome: Applications can reference XML resources by name instead of URL, so the resources can move without breaking links.

today: RFC 3120 is an Informational document that remains in use today. XML.org continues to maintain the xmlorg URN namespace for identifying resources in its repository.

sections.title: XML Resources Need Permanent Names
sections.content:
The XML.org Registry is a public repository where XML schemas, DTDs, stylesheets and other documents can be shared and reused. Documents in the repository need unique, permanent identifiers so that applications can refer to them reliably, even if the physical location or server changes.

This RFC defines a URN (Uniform Resource Name) namespace for assigning such identifiers to XML.org resources. URNs are location-independent names, unlike URLs which point to a specific server.
sections.eli5: Imagine a library where books get moved around. You need a permanent library card number that works no matter which shelf the book is on.

sections.title: How the xmlorg Namespace Works
sections.content:
All URNs in the xmlorg namespace follow the form urn:xmlorg:objects:{type}{:subtype}?:{object-id}. The namespace has one top-level branch called objects. The type field identifies what kind of document it is: schema, dtd, stylesheet, entity, xmlns, or others.

The optional subtype provides additional detail, such as the schema language. The object-id is a unique identifier assigned by the Director of Technical Operations at OASIS. For example: urn:xmlorg:objects:schema:xmlschema:xcatalog or urn:xmlorg:objects:dtd:xml:docbook:v4.1.2.
sections.eli5: A name has a form like urn:xmlorg:objects:schema:xmlschema:mycatalog. Each part tells you what the file is and gives it a unique ID that never changes.

sections.title: Resolution and Use
sections.content:
OASIS distributes catalogs (OASIS TR9401 Catalogs) that map URNs to actual URLs where the resources can be found. A more interactive online resolution service is also planned. The presence of a URN in a catalog indicates that it is valid. URNs are lexically equivalent only if they are exactly identical; there is no special comparison.

Applications and XML tools can use URNs as import statements and entity references, decoupling the XML source from any particular server location.
sections.eli5: OASIS keeps a catalog that says 'this URN can be found at this web address'. When you ask for a resource by name, the catalog tells you where to get it.

references.text: Mealling, M. and R. Daniel, "URI Resolution Services Necessary for URN Resolution", RFC 2483, January 1999.
